previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted after a mechanical fall at home, landing on her left hip. She had multiple recent falls and presented with a large left hip hematoma. Imaging showed no fractures but confirmed soft tissue hematomas. Her hemoglobin dropped from 8.8 to 7.3, prompting a single unit red blood cell transfusion. Cardiac workup was negative for acute ischemia, and telemetry showed no arrhythmias. She remained stable, with no signs of infection despite leukocytosis. Physical therapy recommended inpatient rehabilitation for strength and fall prevention. She was discharged to an extended care facility with continued heart failure management, a reduced allopurinol dose for renal protection, and plans for outpatient follow-up including a contrast CT of the chest to evaluate aortic arch dilation.
problems: Contusion of left hip, initial encounter
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Presence of coronary angioplasty implant and graft
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of breast
Elevated white blood cell count, unspecified
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
